ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, fold the rectangular paper ABCD upwards along AE, so that point B falls at point F on side DC. If $\angle FEC = 28^\circ$, what is the value of $\angle EAB$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By folding, we obtain $\angle BEA = \angle FEA$,\\
$\because \angle FEC = 28^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AEB = (180^\circ - 28^\circ) \div 2 = 76^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle EAB = 90^\circ - \angle AEB = \boxed{14^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/trigonometric route using preserved lengths. Read from the image that A, B, C, D form a rectangle, E lies on vertical side BC, F lies on horizontal side DC, and ∠FEC is the angle between EF and the vertical segment EC. From the text, folding sends B to F along crease AE, so AB = AF and EB = EF. Place coordinates A=(0,0), B=(w,0), C=(w,h), D=(0,h), E=(w,e), F=(f,h). Let θ = ∠EAB, so tan θ = e/w. Since ∠FEC = 28°, the segment EF has horizontal component e sin 28° and vertical component e cos 28° because EF = EB = e; hence f = w − e sin 28° and h = e + e cos 28°. Use AB = AF: w² = f² + h². Substitute f and h, divide by w², and solve for e/w to get e/w = sin 28°/(1 + cos 28°) = tan 14°. Therefore θ = 14°.
